about: LOCK IN's named load rules, one entry per rule, each tied to the code that enforces it. .tools/rulecount.py fails if a rule's code is gone, if a number here differs from the constant in the code, or if any page states a rule count that is not the length of this list. Recounted against 3.9.1005 on 2026-10-21 from the old codex (38 rules, v3.5.156): FLAG A HAND left with the STAGE change on 2026-10-16; STAGE IT, ANCHOR THE SPECIAL HANDLING and HEAVY LEFT HIGH were enforced but not listed; KILLER PAIRS has its own write-up, so it has its own entry.

rules.name: NO FLOATING BOXES
rules.rule: A placement is refused unless three quarters of its bottom cells sit on something, or it is touched on both sides with at least one bottom cell resting. How well the wall is supported multiplies the wall score from 0.6x to 1.0x.

rules.name: SHELF LOCK
rules.rule: Fill all 17 cells of a row and it locks: +500, up to 30 integrity healed, an integrity floor (one shelf 15, two 30, three 45, four 55, five or more 65), and everything at or above it protected from crushing while the row stays full.

rules.name: DOUBLE LOCK
rules.rule: Two locked rows back to back form a bulkhead, which pays a bulkhead bonus that pace scales with the wall.

rules.name: DON'T BREAK YOUR OWN SEAL
rules.rule: Lifting a piece out of a locked shelf unseals it: -150, and the shelf's +500 is gone until it locks again.

rules.name: BRICK THE SEAMS
rules.rule: Four pieces each offset one to three cells from the piece under them earn the wall's one BRICK LOCK, +300. Three or more same-width pieces in a straight column cost 100 per aligned seam.

rules.name: PYRAMID OR IT TOPPLES
rules.rule: A freestanding stack goes over at four pieces, at three unless each piece is narrower than the one under it, at three with a small or a bag in it, and at two once it is taller in cells than its narrowest piece can carry. Flat tires do not count toward it.

rules.name: SKINNY TOWER SNAPS
rules.rule: A pillar two cells wide or narrower and four or more tall, not braced on both sides, carries a thin piece at most half its own height. Past that, the piece on top comes off.

rules.name: HEAVY WANTS A FULL FLOOR
rules.rule: Weight class 4 or more gets no overhang grace: a bottom cell over air and it comes down with what is under it.

rules.name: NO STAIRCASES
rules.rule: An overhang stacked on an overhang comes down. A wide flat slab, at least 2.2 times wider than tall, may overhang.

rules.name: SLIP OR COLLAPSE
rules.rule: One or two pieces coming loose is a slip: -5 integrity, off the record. Three or more is a collapse: -18 integrity, the streak broken, a step on the collapse ladder. Three placements within 15 seconds after it pay +400 RECOVERY.

rules.name: THE WALL HAS AN HP BAR
rules.rule: Integrity drains with unsupported heavies, narrow towers, overhangs, voids and lean, and multiplies the wall score from 0.5x to 1.0x. At 8 or below, the top of the wall sheds a piece or two.

rules.name: KEEP IT CENTERED
rules.rule: A center of gravity more than 15% off the middle drains integrity and costs up to 100, live. Re-balance and it comes back.

rules.name: AIR POCKETS COST RENT
rules.rule: Every covered void costs 8, live.

rules.name: NOTHING HEAVY ON SQUISHY
rules.rule: Weight class 5 set directly on an exposed fragile, small package, bag or hazmat crushes it: -300 each. A box on each side or a locked shelf at or below protects it. The third crushed box in a shift starts the safety ladder.

rules.name: ARROWS POINT UP
rules.rule: A this-side-up box placed rotated costs 16.

rules.name: HAZMAT RIDES LOW
rules.rule: A hazmat above the waist line, the bottom half of the bay, halves the score while it is there and is written up the first time.

rules.name: HAZMAT KEEPS ITS DISTANCE
rules.rule: Different hazard classes stay two clear cells apart, and no more than two pieces of one class touch. Each breach halves the score and is written up the first time. This dock rule is stricter than the federal segregation table for every class on this dock.

rules.name: KILLER PAIRS
rules.rule: The pairs 49 CFR 177.848 keeps apart so a leak cannot mix them (flares with a flammable gas, a flammable liquid or a corrosive liquid; an oxidizer with a flammable liquid or a corrosive liquid) closer than two clear cells, or a corrosive liquid anywhere above an oxidizer, is written up the first time.

rules.name: CAP THE HAZMAT
rules.rule: Locking a shelf over a hazmat loaded low pays +1500.

rules.name: DROP HAZMAT, GO HOME
rules.rule: A hazmat in any slip or collapse, including one swept off with it, ends the round.

rules.name: TIRES LIE FLAT
rules.rule: A tire stood on edge is a safety warning, and anything set on an on-edge tire topples unless the tire is pinned by a locked shelf or braced on both sides.

rules.name: TIRE ON TIRE
rules.rule: A tire set on an on-edge tire: the first time a warning, the second a write-up, the third a practice trailer, the fourth the round ends.

rules.name: A FLAT TIRE IS FURNITURE
rules.rule: Fill a flat tire's hollow with smalls, a bag, a small box or a hazmat for nest pay: 100 plus 150 per cell, 1000 for a hazmat shielded below the waist, 250 per cell more when the stack is full to the rim. A grounded flat tire is a new floor for the stack rules.

rules.name: BAGS ON THE ROOF
rules.rule: A bag of smalls against the ceiling pays +1000. Five of them make a full ceiling course, +2500 more, once per wall.

rules.name: POP THE BAG
rules.rule: Double-click a bag for six gap-fillers: three 2x1 and three 1x1. Smalls and bags never count toward the rate.

rules.name: TAKE THE FRONT PIECE
rules.rule: Reaching past the front of the belt costs 25 per box reached past.

rules.name: FLOW STREAK
rules.rule: Clean fresh placements from the third in a row pay +25, +50, +75 and up. A crush or a collapse resets it; a re-placed piece never counts.

rules.name: SPEED MULTIPLIES THE WALL
rules.rule: The rate multiplies the wall's base score from 0.4x to 4.0x, and the rate counts freight only.

rules.name: THE 250 STANDARD
rules.rule: A sealed wall of six or more boxes loaded under 250 pieces an hour is a productivity flag; every second flag is a write-up.

rules.name: NO STANDING AROUND
rules.rule: Five idle minutes, or a rate under 55 for three minutes, is a strike in TRAILER-LOAD, after a warning.

rules.name: CHURN GETS NOTICED
rules.rule: Picking the same box up again and again escalates to a CHURN write-up, and a re-placed box earns no rate and no streak.

rules.name: WATER IS A PLAY
rules.rule: Four drinks a wall, six seconds apart. Drinks one and two pay +150, the second only with three boxes loaded since the first. No water by 75% of the wall's height is a warning that water washes.

rules.name: THE SAFETY LADDER
rules.rule: A warning repeated before it is washed becomes an incident. A hazmat high, a segregation breach, a killer pair, a crushed hazmat and a second stacked tire are written up at once; every third incident is a write-up. The fifth incident, and each one after it, loads a practice trailer. Four write-ups end the shift.

rules.name: THE DISPATCH CLOCK
rules.rule: At 85% full or 85% high a 60-second clock starts. Seal before zero for up to +800, scaled by the time left and the fill. In TRAILER-LOAD a miss is a strike.

rules.name: BIG FREIGHT DOESN'T RIDE THE BELT
rules.rule: Pieces that cannot ride the belt go to the special-handling rack. A rack of 8 left full is a strike in TRAILER-LOAD, after a warning.

rules.name: FEED THE CHUTE
rules.rule: An empty chute is a jam and BREAK JAM restarts it. Starved 11 seconds in TRAILER-LOAD, the manager breaks it: a strike.

rules.name: THE SEAL GATE
rules.rule: A wall seals at 92% of its height with at least 35% of the bay packed. A full wall is a perfect load.

rules.name: LOOSE WALL, LOOSE PAY
rules.rule: The wall's base pay is fill x 700 plus height x 500, and the +2500 seal payout is multiplied by how solid the wall is.

rules.name: STAGE IT, KEEP THE AISLE CLEAR
rules.rule: A box that does not fit yet can be staged on one of three taped spots. All three full while five more boxes are loaded is an aisle warning. A staged box left on the dock when the run ends costs 100.

rules.name: ANCHOR THE SPECIAL HANDLING
rules.rule: The first special-handling piece on a wall is a CORNERSTONE, +400. One touching two edges is a CORNER LOCK, +350; one edge, a WALL ANCHOR, +150; plugging two or more gaps, a VOID FILLER, +200.

rules.name: HEAVY LEFT HIGH
rules.rule: Heavy freight in the top 40% of the wall with half or less of its base supported, and no locked shelf under it, is a warning at 15 seconds and a strike in TRAILER-LOAD at 30.
